newsitem.title: POLAND: NEW BLOC EMERGES IN POLISH SOLIDARITY ALLIANCE.
newsitem.headline: NEW BLOC EMERGES IN POLISH SOLIDARITY ALLIANCE.

text.p: Ten of the several dozen small right-wing parties comprising the Solidarity Election Action (AWS) on Sunday set up a political bloc ahead of this year's parliamentary elections.
The bloc, the Rightist Accord (PP), at its first congress nominated 150 parliamentary candidates and announced it would remain within the AWS.

The AWS was set up last year as a broadly-based alliance of right-leaning parties clustered around the Solidarity trade union with the avowed purpose of defeating the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).

"Without the AWS one cannot successfully compete with the SLD, but without political parties the AWS cannot effectively oppose the SLD," Jerzy Gwizdz, one of the PP's leaders, said on public television.

AWS deputy chairman Janusz Tomaszewski, a guest at the congress, voiced support for the initiative but said it must lead to a single political formation and a common programme before the elections are held.
Other members of the Solidarity leadership were not immediately available for comment.
The Rightist Accord includes the anti-communist Confederation of Independent Poland (KPN), the Election Solidarity Movement led by Gwizdz and the nationalist National Democratic Party.
